thread:
maya: quick feedback loop — experimenting with an inline-edit mode for capacity controls. rather than steppers, min/max become single-click editable numbers; burst stays as a toggle but we add a keyboard shortcut (b) to open burst details. main goals: faster edits for power users, fewer tab stops for screen reader users.
ravi: sounds promising. question: how do we prevent accidental edits? suggest require Enter to commit and Esc to cancel, and visual focus ring when in edit mode. also show a small undo toast when value changes.
hana: accessibility notes: when an input goes into edit mode announce 'editing min instances' via aria-live and set aria-describedby to helper text. keyboard shortcut 'b' must be discoverable and configurable in user prefs. also ensure inline inputs have role=\"spinbutton\" with aria-valuemin/aria-valuemax/aria-valuenow.
trevor: product thought: popup shortcuts hint in the header (\"press ? for shortcuts\"). for new users keep steppers visible; enable inline-edit in advanced mode or via a user toggle. microcopy: change burst label to 'Temporary burst' and the helper under steppers to 'Targets; autoscaler may exceed briefly' (short).
alex: engineering: inline-edit can be done with contenteditable or input. prefer input[type=number] for predictability and mobile keyboard. commit on Enter, cancel on Esc, support ArrowUp/ArrowDown to increment. we'll need to handle concurrent updates from live autoscaler — optimistic local update then reconcile. small snippet we use elsewhere:
```
<input type=number role=spinbutton aria-valuemin=\"0\" aria-valuemax=\"100\" aria-valuenow=\"2\" />
```
maya: keyboard flow: tab order should be min -> max -> pool -> burst -> slo -> cost. when entering edit mode, trap focus in the number input until commit/cancel. screen readers should read the new value after commit via aria-live.
ravi: discoverability: add a tiny chevron on the burst toggle that briefly pulses on first view and a tooltip that mentions 'press B to open burst details'. also add a small inline latency median next to pool name.
hana: color/accessibility: ensure edit focus ring meets contrast and that the inline value has sufficient contrast for low-vision. SLO slider thumb should have an accessible label and visible tooltip on drag.
trevor: analytics: track how often users switch to inline-edit vs steppers to decide default. also A/B test shortcut visibility.
maya: action items: alex to prototype inline-number input with commit/cancel + ARIA spinbutton semantics; hana to write SR announcement patterns; ravi to mock shortcut hint and pulse affordance; trevor to add metrics to tracking plan; i'll open ticket.
design-bot: created ticket <https://redwood.app/t/RED-5131|RED-5131> 'Inline-edit capacity controls: keyboard shortcut, spinbutton semantics, discovery' :white_check_mark:
alex: i'll push a small prototype branch and link here when ready. :rocket:
maya: great — thanks everyone, let's reconvene after proto review.
